reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend/getDateWithWeekendRule pair and threads holidays through every existing caller instead of adding parallel logic.

duplication.why: The 'holidays ? new Set(holidays) : undefined' conversion is repeated in getNextDate, getDatesInRange, getUpcomingDates and getDateWithSkippedWeekend, and the three daily-skip loops each keep their own branch (now calling the shared predicate).

placement.why: The weekend/holiday rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside the existing weekend helpers; the type field is added to RecurConfig and parseRecurDate.

scope.why: Every edit serves holiday handling; tests are focused.

maintainability.why: One predicate (isWeekendOrHoliday) decides non-business days for both moving and skipping, but its Set parameter versus the array parameter of getDateWithSkippedWeekend makes callers convert in several places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All weekend checks (app.ts daily skips, getNextDate weekday search, the move helper) now go through isWeekendOrHoliday.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated array-to-Set conversion is visible boilerplate, not reshaped logic.

one_place.where: isWeekendOrHoliday in shared/schedules.ts is used by getDateWithSkippedWeekend and by every daily-skip path (getNextDate, getDatesInRange, getUpcomingDates); schedule-template.ts passes holidays to getDateWithWeekendRule.
